1.text: Tha proverbs of Solomon tha son of David, king of Israel;
2 know wisdom N instruction; 2 perceive tha words of understanding;
2 receive tha instruction of wisdom, justice, N judgment, N equity;
2 give subtilty 2 tha simple, 2 tha young man knowledge N discretion.
A wise man will hear, N will increase learning; N a man of understanding shall attain 2 wise counsels:
2 understand a proverb, N tha interpretation; tha words of tha wise, N their dark sayings.
Tha fear of tha LORD is tha beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom N instruction.
My son, hear tha instruction of ur father, N forsake not tha law of ur mother:
4 dey shall be an ornament of grace 2 ur head, N chains about ur neck.
My son, if sinners entice u, consent u not.
If dey say, Come wit us, let us lay wait 4 blood, let us lurk privily 4 tha innocent without cause:
Let us swallow ’em up alive as tha grave; N whole, as dose dat go down in2 tha pit:
We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses wit spoil:
Cast in ur lot among us; let us all have one purse:
My son, walk not u in tha way wit ’em; refrain ur foot from their path:
4 their feet run 2 evil, N make haste 2 shed blood.
Surely in vain tha net is spread in tha sight of any bird.
N dey lay wait 4 their own blood; dey lurk privily 4 their own lives.
So r tha ways of every one dat is greedy of gain; which takes away tha life of tha owners of it.
Wisdom cries without; she utters her voice in tha streets:
She cries in tha chief place of concourse, in tha openings of tha gates: in tha city she utters her words, sayin,
How long, y’all simple ones, will y’all love simplicity? N tha scorners delight in their scorning, N fools hate knowledge?
Turn u at my reproof: look, I will pour out my spirit 2 u, I will make known my words 2 u.
Because I have called, N y’all refused; I have stretched out my hand, N no man regarded;
But y’all have set at nothing all my counsel, N would none of my reproof:
I also will laugh at ur calamity; I will mock when ur fear comes;
When ur fear comes as desolation, N ur destruction comes as a whirlwind; when distress N anguish comes upon u.
Then shall dey call upon me, but I will not answer; dey shall seek me early, but dey shall not find me:
4 dat dey hated knowledge, N did not choose tha fear of tha LORD:
Dey would none of my counsel: dey despised all my reproof.
Therefore shall dey eat of tha fruit of their own way, N be filled wit their own devices.
4 tha turnin away of tha simple shall kill ’em, N tha prosperity of fools shall destroy ’em.
But whoever listens 2 me shall live safely, N shall be quiet from fear of evil.

2.text: My son, if u will receive my words, N hide my commandments wit u;
So dat u incline thine ear 2 wisdom, N apply thine heart 2 understanding;
Yeah, if u criest after knowledge, N lift up ur voice 4 understanding;
If u seek her as silver, N search 4 her as 4 hid treasures;
Then will u understand tha fear of tha LORD, N find tha knowledge of God.
4 tha LORD gives wisdom: out of his mouth comes knowledge N understanding.
He lays up sound wisdom 4 tha righteous: he is a buckler 2 ’em dat walk uprightly.
He keeps tha paths of judgment, N preserves tha way of his saints.
Then will u understand righteousness, N judgment, N equity; yeah, every good path.
When wisdom enters in2 thine heart, N knowledge is pleasant 2 ur soul;
Discretion shall preserve u, understanding shall keep u:
2 deliver u from tha way of tha evil man, from tha man dat speaks froward things;
Who leave tha paths of uprightness, 2 walk in tha ways of darkness;
Who rejoice 2 do evil, N delight in tha frowardness of tha wicked;
Whose ways r crooked, N dey froward in their paths:
2 deliver u from tha strange woman, even from tha stranger which flatters wit her words;
Which forsakes tha guide of her youth, N forgetteth tha covenant of her God.
4 her house inclineth 2 death, N her paths 2 tha dead.
None dat go 2 her return again, neither take dey hold of tha paths of life.
Dat u may walk in tha way of good men, N keep tha paths of tha righteous.
4 tha upright shall live in tha land, N tha perfect shall remain in it.
But tha wicked shall be cut off from tha earth, N tha transgressors shall be rooted out of it.

3.text: My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:
4 length of days, N long life, N peace, shall dey add 2 u.
Don’t let mercy N truth forsake u: bind ’em about ur neck; write ’em upon tha table of thine heart:
So will u find favour N good understanding in tha sight of God N man.
Trust in tha LORD wit all thine heart; N lean not 2 ur own understanding.
In all ur ways acknowledge him, N he shall direct ur paths.
Don’t be wise in ur own eyes: fear tha LORD, N depart from evil.
It shall be health 2 ur navel, N marrow 2 ur bones.
Honour tha LORD wit ur substance, N wit tha firstfruits of all thine increase:
So shall ur barns be filled wit plenty, N ur presses shall burst out wit new wine.
My son, despise not tha chastening of tha LORD; neither be weary of his correction:
4 whom tha LORD loves he correcteth; even as a father tha son in whom he delights.
Happy is tha man dat finds wisdom, N tha man dat gets understanding.
4 tha merchandise of it is better than tha merchandise of silver, N tha gain of it than fine gold.
She is more precious than rubies: N all tha things u can desire r not 2 be compared 2 her.
Length of days is in her right hand; N in her left hand riches N honour.
Her ways r ways of pleasantness, N all her paths r peace.
She is a tree of life 2 ’em dat lay hold upon her: N happy is every one dat retaineth her.
Tha LORD by wisdom has founded tha earth; by understanding has he established tha heavenz.
By his knowledge tha depths r broken up, N tha clouds drop down tha dew.
My son, don’t let ’em depart from ur eyes: keep sound wisdom N discretion:
So shall dey be life 2 ur soul, N grace 2 ur neck.
Then will u walk in ur way safely, N ur foot shall not stumble.
When u lie down, u will not be afraid: yeah, u will lie down, N ur sleep shall be sweet.
Don’t be afraid of sudden fear, neither of tha desolation of tha wicked, when it comes.
4 tha LORD shall be ur confidence, N shall keep ur foot from bein taken.
Withhold not good from ’em 2 whom it is due, when it is in tha power of thine hand 2 do it.
Say not 2 ur neighbour, Go, N come again, N 2 morrow I will give; when u have it by u.
Devise not evil against ur neighbour, seein he lives securely by u.
Strive not wit a man without cause, if he have done u no harm.
Envy u not tha oppressor, N choose none of his ways.
4 tha froward is abomination 2 tha LORD: but his secret is wit tha righteous.
Tha curse of tha LORD is in tha house of tha wicked: but he blesses tha habitation of tha just.
Surely he scorneth tha scorners: but he gives grace 2 tha lowly.
Tha wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be tha promotion of fools.

4.text: Hear, y’all children, tha instruction of a father, N attend 2 know understanding.
4 I give u good doctrine, forsake y’all not my law.
4 I was my father’s son, tender N only beloved in tha sight of my mother.
He taught me also, N said 2 me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, N live.
Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from tha words of my mouth.
Forsake her not, N she shall preserve u: love her, N she shall keep u.
Wisdom is tha principal thing; therefore get wisdom: N wit all ur getting get understanding.
Exalt her, N she shall promote u: she shall bring u 2 honour, when u do embrace her.
She shall give 2 thine head an ornament of grace: a crown of glory shall she deliver 2 u.
Hear, O my son, N receive my sayings; N tha years of ur life shall be many.
I have taught u in tha way of wisdom; I have led u in right paths.
When u go, ur steps shall not be straitened; N when u run, u will not stumble.
Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; 4 she is ur life.
Enter not in2 tha path of tha wicked, N go not in tha way of evil men.
Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, N pass away.
4 dey sleep not, except dey have done mischief; N their sleep is taken away, unless dey cause some 2 fall.
4 dey eat tha bread of wickedness, N drink tha wine of violence.
But tha path of tha just is as tha shinin light, dat shines more N more 2 tha perfect day.
Tha way of tha wicked is as darkness: dey know not at what dey stumble.
My son, attend 2 my words; incline thine ear 2 my sayings.
Let ’em not depart from ur eyes; keep ’em in tha midst of thine heart.
4 dey r life 2 dose dat find ’em, N health 2 all their flesh.
Keep ur heart wit all diligence; 4 out of it r tha issues of life.
Put away from u a froward mouth, N perverse lips put far from u.
Let ur eyes look right on, N let thine eyelids look straight before u.
Ponder tha path of ur feet, N let all ur ways be established.
Turn not 2 tha right hand nor 2 tha left: remove ur foot from evil.

5.text: My son, attend 2 my wisdom, N bow thine ear 2 my understanding:
Dat u may regard discretion, N dat ur lips may keep knowledge.
4 tha lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, N her mouth is smoother than oil:
But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.
Her feet go down 2 death; her steps take hold on hell.
Lest u should ponder tha path of life, her ways r moveable, dat u can not know ’em.
Hear me now therefore, O y’all children, N depart not from tha words of my mouth.
Remove ur way far from her, N come not nigh tha door of her house:
Lest u give thine honour 2 others, N ur years 2 tha cruel:
Lest strangers be filled wit ur wealth; N ur labours be in tha house of a stranger;
N u mourn at tha last, when ur flesh N ur body r consumed,
N say, How have I hated instruction, N my heart despised reproof;
N have not obeyed tha voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear 2 ’em dat instructed me!
I was almost in all evil in tha midst of tha congregation N assembly.
Drink waterz out of ur own cistern, N runnin waterz out of ur own well.
Let ur fountains be dispersed abroad, N rivers of waterz in tha streets.
Let ’em be only ur own, N not strangers’ wit u.
Let ur fountain be blessed: N rejoice wit tha wife of ur youth.
Let her be as tha lovin hind N pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy u at all times; N be u ravished always wit her love.
N why will u, my son, be ravished wit a strange woman, N embrace tha bosom of a stranger?
4 tha ways of man r before tha eyes of tha LORD, N he pondereth all his goings.
His own iniquities shall take tha wicked himself, N he shall be holden wit tha cords of his sins.
He shall die without instruction; N in tha greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

6.text: My son, if u be surety 4 ur friend, if u have stricken ur hand wit a stranger,
u r snared wit tha words of ur mouth, u r taken wit tha words of ur mouth.
Do dis now, my son, N deliver urself, when u r come in2 tha hand of ur friend; go, humble urself, N make sure ur friend.
Give not sleep 2 ur eyes, nor slumber 2 thine eyelids.
Deliver urself as a roe from tha hand of tha hunter, N as a bird from tha hand of tha fowler.
Go 2 tha ant, u sluggard; consider her ways, N be wise:
Which havin no guide, overseer, or ruler,
Provideth her food in tha summer, N gathers her food in tha harvest.
How long will u sleep, O sluggard? when will u arise out of ur sleep?
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of tha hands 2 sleep:
So shall ur poverty come as one dat travelleth, N ur want as an armed man.
A naughty person, a wicked man, walks wit a froward mouth.
He winketh wit his eyes, he speaks wit his feet, he teaches wit his fingers;
Frowardness is in his heart, he devises mischief continually; he sows discord.
Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy.
Dese six things does tha LORD hate: yeah, seven r an abomination 2 him:
A proud look, a lyin tongue, N hands dat shed innocent blood,
An heart dat devises wicked imaginations, feet dat be swift in runnin 2 mischief,
A false witness dat speaks lies, N he dat sows discord among brothers.
My son, keep ur father’s commandment, N forsake not tha law of ur mother:
Bind ’em continually upon thine heart, N tie ’em about ur neck.
When u go, it shall lead u; when u sleep, it shall keep u; N when u awakest, it shall talk wit u.
4 tha commandment is a lamp; N tha law is light; N reproofs of instruction r tha way of life:
2 keep u from tha evil woman, from tha flattery of tha tongue of a strange woman.
Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take u wit her eyelids.
4 by means of a whorish woman a man is brought 2 a piece of bread: N tha adulteress will hunt 4 tha precious life.
Can a man take fire in his bosom, N his clothes not be burned?
Can one go upon hot coals, N his feet not be burned?
So he dat goes in 2 his neighbour’s wife; whoever touches her shall not be innocent.
Men do not despise a thief, if he steal 2 satisfy his soul when he is hungry;
But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all tha substance of his house.
But whoever commits adultery wit a woman lacketh understanding: he dat does it destroys his own soul.
A wound N dishonour shall he get; N his reproach shall not be wiped away.
4 jealousy is tha rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in tha day of vengeance.
He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though u give many gifts.

7.text: My son, keep my words, N lay up my commandments wit u.
Keep my commandments, N live; N my law as tha apple of thine eye.
Bind ’em upon ur fingers, write ’em upon tha table of thine heart.
Say 2 wisdom, u r my sister; N call understanding ur kinswoman:
Dat dey may keep u from tha strange woman, from tha stranger which flatters wit her words.
4 at tha window of my house I looked through my casement,
N beheld among tha simple ones, I discerned among tha youths, a young man void of understanding,
Passing through tha street near her corner; N he went tha way 2 her house,
In tha twilight, in tha evening, in tha black N dark night:
N, look, there met him a woman wit tha attire of an harlot, N subtil of heart.
(She is loud N stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:
Now is she without, now in tha streets, N lies in wait at every corner.)
So she caught him, N kissed him, N wit an impudent face said 2 him,
I have peace offerings wit me; dis day have I payed my vows.
Therefore came I forth 2 meet u, diligently 2 seek ur face, N I have found u.
I have decked my bed wit coverings of tapestry, wit carved works, wit fine linen of Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed wit myrrh, aloes, N cinnamon.
Come, let us take our fill of love until tha morning: let us solace ourselves wit loves.
4 tha goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey:
He has taken a bag of money wit him, N will come home at tha day appointed.
Wit her much fair speech she caused him 2 yield, wit tha flattering of her lips she forced him.
He goes after her right away, as an ox goes 2 tha slaughter, or as a fool 2 tha correction of tha stocks;
Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hurries 2 tha snare, N knows not dat it is 4 his life.
Listen 2 me now therefore, O y’all children, N attend 2 tha words of my mouth.
Don’t let thine heart decline 2 her ways, go not astray in her paths.
4 she has cast down many wounded: yeah, many strong men have been killed by her.
Her house is tha way 2 hell, goin down 2 tha chambers of death.

8.text: Does not wisdom cry? N understanding put forth her voice?
She stands in tha top of high places, by tha way in tha places of tha paths.
She cries at tha gates, at tha entry of tha city, at tha comin in at tha doors.
2 u, O men, I call; N my voice is 2 tha sons of man.
O y’all simple, understand wisdom: N, y’all fools, be y’all of an understanding heart.
Hear; 4 I will speak of excellent things; N tha opening of my lips shall be right things.
4 my mouth shall speak truth; N wickedness is an abomination 2 my lips.
All tha words of my mouth r in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in ’em.
Dey r all plain 2 him dat understands, N right 2 ’em dat find knowledge.
Receive my instruction, N not silver; N knowledge rather than choice gold.
4 wisdom is better than rubies; N all tha things dat may be desired r not 2 be compared 2 it.
I wisdom live wit prudence, N find out knowledge of witty inventions.
Tha fear of tha LORD is 2 hate evil: pride, N arrogancy, N tha evil way, N tha froward mouth, do I hate.
Counsel is mine, N sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength.
By me kings reign, N princes decree justice.
By me princes rule, N nobles, even all tha judges of tha earth.
I love ’em dat love me; N dose dat seek me early shall find me.
Riches N honour r wit me; yeah, durable riches N righteousness.
My fruit is better than gold, yeah, than fine gold; N my revenue than choice silver.
I lead in tha way of righteousness, in tha midst of tha paths of judgment:
Dat I may cause dose dat love me 2 inherit substance; N I will fill their treasures.
Tha LORD possessed me in tha beginning of his way, before his works of old.
I was set up from everlasting, from tha beginning, or ever tha earth was.
When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding wit water.
Before tha mountains were settled, before tha hills was I brought forth:
While as yet he had not made tha earth, nor tha fields, nor tha highest part of tha dust of tha world.
When he prepared tha heavenz, I was there: when he set a compass upon tha face of tha depth:
When he established tha clouds above: when he strengthened tha fountains of tha deep:
When he gave 2 tha sea his decree, dat tha waterz should not pass his commandment: when he appointed tha foundations of tha earth:
Then I was by him, as one brought up wit him: N I was daily his delight, rejoicin always before him;
Rejoicin in tha habitable part of his earth; N my delights were wit tha sons of men.
Now therefore listen 2 me, O y’all children: 4 blessed r dey dat keep my ways.
Hear instruction, N be wise, N refuse it not.
Blessed is tha man dat hears me, watchin daily at my gates, waitin at tha posts of my doors.
4 whoever finds me finds life, N shall obtain favour of tha LORD.
But he dat sins against me wrongeth his own soul: all dey dat hate me love death.

9.text: Wisdom has builded her house, she has hewn out her seven pillars:
She has killed her beasts; she has mingled her wine; she has also furnished her table.
She has sent forth her maidens: she cries upon tha highest places of tha city,
Whoever is simple, let him turn in here: as 4 him dat wants understanding, she says 2 him,
Come, eat of my bread, N drink of tha wine which I have mingled.
Forsake tha foolish, N live; N go in tha way of understanding.
He dat reproveth a scorner gets 2 himself shame: N he dat rebuketh a wicked man gets himself a blot.
Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate u: rebuke a wise man, N he will love u.
Give instruction 2 a wise man, N he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, N he will increase in learning.
Tha fear of tha LORD is tha beginning of wisdom: N tha knowledge of tha holy is understanding.
4 by me ur days shall be multiplied, N tha years of ur life shall be increased.
If u be wise, u will be wise 4 urself: but if u scornest, u alone will bear it.
A foolish woman is clamorous: she is simple, N knows nothing.
4 she sits at tha door of her house, on a seat in tha high places of tha city,
2 call passengers who go right on their ways:
Whoever is simple, let him turn in here: N as 4 him dat wants understanding, she says 2 him,
Stolen waterz r sweet, N bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
But he knows not dat tha dead r there; N dat her guests r in tha depths of hell.

10.text: Tha proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father: but a foolish son is tha heaviness of his mother.
Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivers from death.
Tha LORD will not suffer tha soul of tha righteous 2 famish: but he casts away tha substance of tha wicked.
He becomes poor dat deals wit a slack hand: but tha hand of tha diligent makes rich.
He dat gathers in summer is a wise son: but he dat sleeps in harvest is a son dat causes shame.
Blessings r upon tha head of tha just: but violence covers tha mouth of tha wicked.
Tha memory of tha just is blessed: but tha name of tha wicked shall rot.
Tha wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.
He dat walks uprightly walks surely: but he dat perverteth his ways shall be known.
He dat winketh wit tha eye causes sorrow: but a prating fool shall fall.
Tha mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covers tha mouth of tha wicked.
Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covers all sins.
In tha lips of him dat has understanding wisdom is found: but a rod is 4 tha back of him dat is void of understanding.
Wise men lay up knowledge: but tha mouth of tha foolish is near destruction.
Tha rich man’s wealth is his strong city: tha destruction of tha poor is their poverty.
Tha labour of tha righteous tendeth 2 life: tha fruit of tha wicked 2 sin.
He is in tha way of life dat keeps instruction: but he dat refuses reproof erreth.
He dat hides hatred wit lyin lips, N he dat utters a slander, is a fool.
In tha crowd of words there wants not sin: but he dat refraineth his lips is wise.
Tha tongue of tha just is as choice silver: tha heart of tha wicked is little worth.
Tha lips of tha righteous feed many: but fools die 4 want of wisdom.
Tha blessing of tha LORD, it makes rich, N he addeth no sorrow wit it.
It is as sport 2 a fool 2 do mischief: but a man of understanding has wisdom.
Tha fear of tha wicked, it shall come upon him: but tha desire of tha righteous shall be granted.
As tha whirlwind passes, so is tha wicked no more: but tha righteous is an everlasting foundation.
As vinegar 2 tha teeth, N as smoke 2 tha eyes, so is tha sluggard 2 ’em dat send him.
Tha fear of tha LORD prolongeth days: but tha years of tha wicked shall be shortened.
Tha hope of tha righteous shall be gladness: but tha expectation of tha wicked shall perish.
Tha way of tha LORD is strength 2 tha upright: but destruction shall be 2 tha workers of iniquity.
Tha righteous shall never be removed: but tha wicked shall not inhabit tha earth.
Tha mouth of tha just brings forth wisdom: but tha froward tongue shall be cut out.
Tha lips of tha righteous know what is acceptable: but tha mouth of tha wicked speaks frowardness.

11.text: A false balance is abomination 2 tha LORD: but a just weight is his delight.
When pride comes, then comes shame: but wit tha lowly is wisdom.
Tha integrity of tha upright shall guide ’em: but tha perverseness of transgressors shall destroy ’em.
Riches profit not in tha day of wrath: but righteousness delivers from death.
Tha righteousness of tha perfect shall direct his way: but tha wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.
Tha righteousness of tha upright shall deliver ’em: but transgressors shall be taken in their own naughtiness.
When a wicked man dies, his expectation shall perish: N tha hope of unjust men perishes.
Tha righteous is delivered out of trouble, N tha wicked comes in his stead.
An hypocrite wit his mouth destroys his neighbour: but through knowledge shall tha just be delivered.
When it goes well wit tha righteous, tha city rejoices: N when tha wicked perish, there is shouting.
By tha blessing of tha upright tha city is exalted: but it is overthrown by tha mouth of tha wicked.
He dat is void of wisdom despiseth his neighbour: but a man of understanding holds his peace.
A talebearer reveals secrets: but he dat is of a faithful spirit concealeth tha matter.
Where no counsel is, tha people fall: but in tha crowd of counsellors there is safety.
He dat is surety 4 a stranger shall smart 4 it: N he dat hates suretiship is sure.
A gracious woman retaineth honour: N strong men retain riches.
Tha merciful man does good 2 his own soul: but he dat is cruel troubles his own flesh.
Tha wicked works a deceitful work: but 2 him dat sows righteousness shall be a sure reward.
As righteousness tendeth 2 life: so he dat pursues evil pursues it 2 his own death.
Dey dat r of a froward heart r abomination 2 tha LORD: but such as r upright in their way r his delight.
Though hand join in hand, tha wicked shall not be unpunished: but tha seed of tha righteous shall be delivered.
As a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.
Tha desire of tha righteous is only good: but tha expectation of tha wicked is wrath.
There is dat scatters, N yet increases; N there is dat withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth 2 poverty.
Tha liberal soul shall be made fat: N he dat watereth shall be watered also himself.
He dat withholdeth corn, tha people shall curse him: but blessing shall be upon tha head of him dat sells it.
He dat diligently seeks good procureth favour: but he dat seeks mischief, it shall come 2 him.
He dat trusts in his riches shall fall: but tha righteous shall flourish as a branch.
He dat troubles his own house shall inherit tha wind: N tha fool shall be servant 2 tha wise of heart.
Tha fruit of tha righteous is a tree of life; N he dat winneth souls is wise.
Look, tha righteous shall be recompensed in tha earth: much more tha wicked N tha sinner.

12.text: Whoever loves instruction loves knowledge: but he dat hates reproof is brutish.
A good man obtaineth favour of tha LORD: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.
A man shall not be established by wickedness: but tha root of tha righteous shall not be moved.
A virtuous woman is a crown 2 her husband: but she dat makes ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.
Tha thoughts of tha righteous r right: but tha counsels of tha wicked r deceit.
Tha words of tha wicked r 2 lie in wait 4 blood: but tha mouth of tha upright shall deliver ’em.
Tha wicked r overthrown, N r not: but tha house of tha righteous shall stand.
A man shall be commended according 2 his wisdom: but he dat is of a perverse heart shall be despised.
He dat is despised, N has a servant, is better than he dat honors himself, N lacketh bread.
A righteous man regards tha life of his beast: but tha tender mercies of tha wicked r cruel.
He dat tilleth his land shall be satisfied wit bread: but he dat follows vain persons is void of understanding.
Tha wicked desires tha net of evil men: but tha root of tha righteous yieldeth fruit.
Tha wicked is snared by tha transgression of his lips: but tha just shall come out of trouble.
A man shall be satisfied wit good by tha fruit of his mouth: N tha recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered 2 him.
Tha way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he dat listens 2 counsel is wise.
A fool’s wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covers shame.
He dat speaks truth shows forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.
There is dat speaks like tha piercings of a sword: but tha tongue of tha wise is health.
Tha lip of truth shall be established 4 ever: but a lyin tongue is but 4 a moment.
Deceit is in tha heart of ’em dat imagine evil: but 2 tha counsellors of peace is joy.
There shall no evil happen 2 tha just: but tha wicked shall be filled wit mischief.
Lyin lips r abomination 2 tha LORD: but dey dat deal truly r his delight.
A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but tha heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.
Tha hand of tha diligent shall bear rule: but tha slothful shall be under tribute.
Heaviness in tha heart of man makes it stoop: but a good word makes it glad.
Tha righteous is more excellent than his neighbour: but tha way of tha wicked seduceth ’em.
Tha slothful man roasteth not dat which he took in hunting: but tha substance of a diligent man is precious.
In tha way of righteousness is life; N in tha pathway of it there is no death.

13.text: A wise son hears his father’s instruction: but a scorner hears not rebuke.
A man shall eat good by tha fruit of his mouth: but tha soul of tha transgressors shall eat violence.

Tha ransom of a man’s life r his riches: but tha poor hears not rebuke.
Tha light of tha righteous rejoices: but tha lamp of tha wicked shall be put out.
Only by pride comes contention: but wit tha well advised is wisdom.

Tha law of tha wise is a fountain of life, 2 depart from tha snares of death.

Tha desire accomplished is sweet 2 tha soul: but it is abomination 2 fools 2 depart from evil.

14.text: Every wise woman builds her house: but tha foolish plucketh it down wit her hands.

15.text: A soft answer turns away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

All tha days of tha afflicted r evil: but he dat is of a merry heart has a continual feast.

16.text: Tha preparations of tha heart in man, N tha answer of tha tongue, is from tha LORD.

A violent man enticeth his neighbour, N leads him in2 tha way dat is not good.
He shuts his eyes 2 devise froward things: movin his lips he brings evil 2 pass.

Tha lot is cast in2 tha lap; but tha whole disposing of it is of tha LORD.

17.text: Better is a dry morsel, N quietness wit it, than an house full of sacrifices wit strife.

18.text: Through desire a man, havin separated himself, seeks N intermeddleth wit all wisdom.

22.text: A good name is rather 2 be chosen than great riches, N lovin favour rather than silver N gold.

23.text: When u sit 2 eat wit a ruler, consider diligently what is before u:

If u faint in tha day of adversity, ur strength is small.

If u sayest, look, we knew it not; does not he dat pondereth tha heart consider it? N he dat keeps ur soul, does not he know it? N shall not he render 2 every man according 2 his works?
My son, eat u honey, because it is good; N tha honeycomb, which is sweet 2 ur taste:

Lay not wait, O wicked man, against tha livin of tha righteous; spoil not his resting place:
4 a just man falls seven times, N rises up again: but tha wicked shall fall in2 mischief.
Rejoice not when thine opp falls, N don’t let thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
Lest tha LORD see it, N it displease him, N he turn away his wrath from him.

4 there shall be no reward 2 tha evil man; tha candle of tha wicked shall be put out.
My son, fear u tha LORD N tha king: N meddle not wit ’em dat r given 2 change:

Dese things also belong 2 tha wise. It is not good 2 have respect of persons in judgment.

But 2 ’em dat rebuke him shall be delight, N a good blessing shall come upon ’em.

Prepare ur work without, N make it fit 4 urself in tha field; N afterwards build thine house.
Don’t be a witness against ur neighbour without cause; N deceive not wit ur lips.

I went by tha field of tha slothful, N by tha vineyard of tha man void of understanding;
N, look, it was all grown over wit thorns, N nettles had covered tha face of it, N tha stone wall of it was broken down.
Then I saw, N considered it well: I looked upon it, N received instruction.
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of tha hands 2 sleep:

25.text: Dese r also proverbs of Solomon, which tha men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

4 better it is dat it be said 2 u, Come up here; than dat u should be put lower in tha presence of tha prince whom ur eyes have seen.

26.text: As snow in summer, N as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly 4 a fool.

As a mad man who casts firebrands, arrows, N death,

27.text: Boast not urself of 2 morrow; 4 u know not what a day may bring forth.

Ur own friend, N ur father’s friend, forsake not; neither go in2 ur brother’s house in tha day of ur calamity: 4 better is a neighbour dat is near than a brother far off.

4 riches r not 4 ever: N does tha crown endure 2 every generation?

28.text: Tha wicked flee when no man pursues: but tha righteous r bold as a lion.

Whoever causes tha righteous 2 go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself in2 his own pit: but tha upright shall have good things in possession.

A man dat does violence 2 tha blood of any person shall flee 2 tha pit; let no man stay him.

2 have respect of persons is not good: 4 4 a piece of bread dat man will transgress.

Whoever robbeth his father or his mother, N says, It is no transgression; tha same is tha companion of a destroyer.

29.text: He, dat bein often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, N dat without remedy.

30.text: Tha words of Agur tha son of Jakeh, even tha prophecy: tha man spoke 2 Ithiel, even 2 Ithiel N Ucal,

Tha grave; N tha barren womb; tha earth dat is not filled wit water; N tha fire dat says not, It is enough.

4 three things tha earth is disquieted, N 4 four which it cannot bear:
4 a servant when he reigns; N a fool when he is filled wit food;
4 an odious woman when she is married; N an handmaid dat is heir 2 her mistress.

Tha ants r a people not strong, yet dey prepare their food in tha summer;
Tha conies r but a feeble folk, yet make dey their houses in tha rocks;
